options.text: Nothing — arrays are not valid input to from

questions.explanation: from iterates its input, so an array becomes three emissions. To emit the array itself as a single value you would use of([1, 2, 3]).

options.text: timer(2000) emits 0 once after 2s then completes; timer(2000, 1000) emits 0 after 2s then 1,2,3… every 1s forever
timer(2000) emits every 2s; timer(2000, 1000) emits every 1000s
timer(2000) errors because it needs two arguments

questions.explanation: A single-argument timer emits 0 after the due time and completes. Adding a period makes it repeat (1, 2, 3, …) on that interval and never complete.

questions.prompt: Which of these creation sources do NOT complete on their own? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: fromEvent and interval are open-ended and never self-complete — you must unsubscribe or use a completing operator. of and range emit their values and then complete.
range(start, count) emits `count` integers starting at `start`. So range(5, 3) emits 5, 6, 7 — the second argument is a count, not an end value.

questions.prompt: In RxJS 7, complete this so it errors immediately: `throwError(() => new Error('x'))`. The argument you pass to throwError is called an error ______ (one word).
questions.explanation: RxJS 7 expects an error factory — a function that returns the error — so `throwError(() => new Error('x'))`. Passing the error directly is the deprecated form.

questions.explanation: of emits its arguments; EMPTY completes with nothing; interval counts up forever; defer calls its factory per subscription for a fresh source.
